title: Token Cost Forensics: Drill-down anomaly inspector & CSV recipe exporter
creator: Lena Thompson
description:
Problem: Customers struggle to diagnose sudden jumps in token spend because current cost views surface aggregate totals but not the forensic trail (attribution rules, prompt prefixes, model fallbacks, cached prefixes). This ticket scopes a design prototype for a Token Cost Forensics panel in the Redwood Console that combines interactive drill-downs, lightweight anomaly detection indicators, and a CSV "recipe" export that captures the attribution rules and filters used to reproduce the view programmatically.

Goals: 
- Provide a compact inspector UI that surfaces the top contributing factors for a selected time window (prompt buckets, model variants, sequence-length bands, cache hit/miss).
- Make anomalies explicit with signal-driven badges (spike, regression, outlier) and clickable context that links to the raw traces and the rollout config used at the time.
- Allow operators to export a reproducible CSV "recipe": metadata (time window, model id/version, quantization profile), attribution parameters (prefix heuristics, per-route cost weights), and a mapping of token buckets to user-visible labels. The CSV should be human-readable and consumable by analytics pipelines.
- Surface recommended next steps (canary rollback, adjust batching or cache TTL) based on detected root causes and historical impact.

Scope (MVP): 
- New panel under Console > Cost Insights: "Forensics" tab with sparkline timeline, top 5 contributors list, and anomalous-segment timeline scrubber.
- Detail flyout for a single anomalous segment showing attribution breakdown by: model variant, prompt template, average seq len, cache hit rate, and route.
- CSV recipe export with schema header and example row, plus a JSON attachment option for programmatic replay (note: JSON export will be an engineering follow-up).
- Accessibility review and keyboard-first interactions for the flyout.

Non-goals: 
- Heavy ML anomaly training in this ticket (we rely on existing anomaly signal from Observability infra).
- Full pipeline replay in the UI (export only creates recipe; playback handled by downstream automation).

Trade-offs considered: 
- Inline vs flyout details: we evaluated embedding more cells in the table but decided on flyouts to keep the list scannable and avoid cognitive overload.
- CSV-first vs JSON-first export: CSV chosen for MVP because customers requested a spreadsheet-friendly artifact for SLAs and finance reconciliation; JSON replay will be added in ENG follow-up.
- Attribution transparency vs clutter: we will show the attribution algorithm summary (top-level formula + tunable knobs) and expose an "advanced" section for full rule listings to keep the view approachable for product owners.

Deliverables: 
- High-fidelity Figma prototype of the Forensics panel (desktop, 1200px content width) with annotated interaction flows.
- Clickable demo recording (30-60s) for PM/Eng review.
- CSV schema doc and an example export that includes reproduceable attribution recipe fields.
- Usability test plan and 5-user remote moderated sessions with billing and platform customers.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Designers and Eng agree on component APIs for the timeline scrubber, contributor list, and flyout (link to notes).
- Prototype demonstrates exporting a CSV recipe containing at minimum: timestamp range, model id/version, quantization tag, attribution heuristics summary, top contributor keys and token counts, and the console route id.
- Usability test run completed with at least 4/5 participants able to (a) identify the root cause contributor for a simulated spend spike and (b) export a CSV recipe without facilitator help.
- All UI strings reviewed by Content Design and pass accessibility contrast and keyboard navigation checks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Component API sign-off from Eng + PM documented in notes link. 2) Prototype CSV export contains schema header and example row. 3) Usability testing: 4/5 participants complete root-cause & export tasks. 4) Accessibility checklist passed for contrast and keyboard interactions.
